chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from his father Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who gives charity to some of his children with a portion of his wealth, and then it occurs to him afterwards to include another of his children with them. He said, 'There is no harm in that.'

And [asked] about a man who gives charity with some of his wealth to some of his children and specifies it for them; is it permissible for him to include others of his children with them after he has specified it for them through charity? He said, 'It is not for him to do so, unless he stipulates that whoever is born is like the one who was given charity, and that is for him.'
ai.seo_question: Can a father include other children in a charity gift he already gave to one child?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between a general endowment (*sadaqah mutlaqah*) and a specific bequest (*hibah* with conditions) regarding a father's gifts to his offspring. It establishes that while a father may freely include other children in a general gift, he must explicitly stipulate that future-born children are included to extend the benefit to them, reflecting the Shia emphasis on contractual clarity in family wealth distribution. This ruling ensures fairness among heirs and prevents unilateral changes to the status of specific gifts, aligning with the principle of *istihsan* (juridical preference) in Twelver fiqh.
